answer:
- **Advanced OCR**: Planned for general release in **August 2026** as **v2.8.0**, targeted for **August 25, 2026** [NL-014#NL-014-S03]. It is scheduled as a standard component of the KnowledgeHub ingestion layer [NL-014#NL-014-S06]. Availability is plan-tiered: included natively in the **Enterprise plan**, offered as a **paid add-on for Growth plans ($500/month)**, and **not supported on the Starter plan** [NL-014#NL-014-S06].

- **WorkflowCoach public beta**: Official target is **September 2026** as **v2.9.0**, targeted for **September 29, 2026** [NL-014#NL-014-S03]. It is planned for **all active Growth and Enterprise accounts** [NL-014#NL-014-S05]. However, dependencies on the Advanced OCR Pipeline and permission synchronization may delay the public beta to **November 2026**, and the CTO’s realistic estimate is that the release should move to November 2026 [NL-014#NL-014-S05][NL-015#NL-015-S05]. A private beta was already running for about 11% of customers [NL-014#NL-014-S05].

- **Teams connector**: Still **under active design and planning**, with a release target of **Q4 2026 (v2.11.0, November release)** [NL-014#NL-014-S07]. A **restricted pilot begins October 2026** with selected financial and healthcare accounts; it is not generally available yet, and only the Slack connector exists as a limited pilot [NL-014#NL-014-S07]. It also carries third-party API risk from Microsoft Graph changes [NL-014#NL-014-S09].

In contrast, Advanced OCR is the earliest general release and is tiered by plan; WorkflowCoach public beta is officially September but may slip to November and targets all Growth/Enterprise accounts; the Teams connector is the latest, planned for November with only a pilot in October.
